text:
maria: quick thought — we keep hitting complexity with explicit resume tokens for streaming across region failover. proposal: implicit checkpoints tied to the connection lease (lease_id + offset) surfaced as a signed header. simpler for most clients, avoids long-lived tokens. thoughts?

jon: sounds interesting. main worry is side-effects (tool calls) — when do we consider a stream replay safe?

maria: good call. plan is: implicit checkpoint for pure read streams (text) only. for any side-effectful paths we require explicit idempotency-key or client-managed token.

prakash: how do we move the checkpoint when proxy A → proxy B handoff happens during failover? lease is connection-scoped. new connection = new lease. we need a transfer mechanism or we accept a window where resume isn't possible.

maria: we can surface a compact signed checkpoint header that encodes (lease_epoch, offset, sample_hash) and is verifiable by downstream proxies. if downstream can't verify, fallback to full token or restart.

anya: signed header implies key management. for Hosted we'd sign at edge with short-lived keys; for Private customers they'd want to sign with their KMS/HSM or we need a compatibility mode. ops overhead?

infra-bot: NOTE: changing headers will require gateway rollout + SDK updates. Recommend feature-flag rollout.

jon: also think about observability — add histograms for checkpoint-gap, resume-attempts, resume-success-rate, and a tracing tag with checkpoint_id. SLO risk?

maria: SLO risk low for reads. For any operation with external side effects we block implicit resume and rely on explicit idempotency validation. we'll run a canary before broad rollout.

prakash: edge impl notes: keep header tiny. suggestion: 
``` 
X-RW-Checkpoint: v1|epoch:4|off:123456|sig:BASE64
sig = HMAC-SHA256(short_lived_key, lease_id + ':' + epoch + ':' + off)
```
Verification: proxies accept if sig validates and epoch within window. otherwise decline and mark as unverifiable.

anya: SDK behavior: auto-retry with checkpoint only if SDK sees header+200 and stream ended early. otherwise expose to app to decide. docs need to be explicit about side-effects.

jon: migration plan? clients that rely on explicit tokens should keep working. we need server-side fallback: if no checkpoint header or unverifiable, fall back to token-based resume or full restart.

maria: yes. RFC checklist I'm thinking: design doc, interop tests (nginx/fastly style termination), telemetry, SDK changes, canary plan (5% → 25% → 100%), opt-out for Private. I'll open PR.

prakash: one more: rate-limiting + backpressure. checkpoints shouldn't let a resumed stream bypass admission controls. we must re-evaluate admission at resume time and possibly queue.

maria: agreed — resume must re-check admission tokens and quotas. record that in the RFC.

infra-bot: ACTION: canary job created (flag:stream-checkpoint-lease). schedule: canary starts in 24h for 6h window.

anya: okay, I'll draft the SDK section and migration notes.

maria: thanks — will open RFC PR today. @jon can you whip up the dashboard tiles?

jon: will do, adding checkpoint metrics to the streaming dashboard. :+1:
